title: SeqShot snapshot runner with quantile-stitching reporter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds SeqShot snapshot runner and a quantile-stitching reporter for composite tail analysis; intended for targeted regression hunts and profiling runs.
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight runner that produces compact, timestamped snapshots of inference traffic across multiple sequence-length cohorts so that downstream reporters can stitch quantile curves across windows. Existing runners either emit full traces (too heavy) or only cumulative metrics (too coarse). This PR introduces 'SeqShot', a snapshot runner that samples short, aligned time-slices across cohorts, and a 'quantile-stitching' reporter that merges per-window histograms into a smooth composite latency quantile curve suitable for regression diffing and visualization.

What this changes (single continuous body): Adds a new bench harness (SeqShot) that performs synchronized short-lived probes across specified cohort buckets (seq-length, payload size, model variant). Snapshots include per-request metadata (cohort id, seed, trace-id), latency histograms, and optional kernel-level tags. The reporter consumes snapshot batches and performs an overlap-aware stitching algorithm that glues adjacent window histograms using weighted interpolation to produce a global quantile curve resilient to out-of-order snapshots and transient spikes.

Checklist: - [x] Implement SeqShot runner with seeding and deterministic replay mode - [x] Implement quantile-stitching reporter with configurable overlap factor - [x] Add unit tests for stitching logic and histogram merge edge cases - [x] Add end-to-end integration test that runs SeqShot against the local micro-bench env - [x] Benchmarked on a microburst and steady-state scenario, results attached in artifacts - [x] Updated README and runner docs

High-level commits summary: Commit 1: Add seqshot runner scaffolding and CLI flags (seed, window, overlap, cohorts) Commit 2: Implement snapshot serializer and compact on-disk format (snappy compressed JSONL) Commit 3: Quantile-stitching algorithm and fast histogram merge utilities Commit 4: Integration test harness and CI job Commit 5: Docs, examples, and minor perf fixes

Changed files (high level): - benchmark-lab/seqshot/runner.py - benchmark-lab/seqshot/serializer.py - benchmark-lab/reporters/quantile_stitching.py - benchmark-lab/reporters/_histogram_utils.py - benchmark-lab/tests/test_seqshot_integration.py - benchmark-lab/tests/test_quantile_stitching.py - benchmark-lab/ci/bench-e2e.yml - docs/benchmark-lab/seqshot.md - examples/seqshot/run_shot.sh - examples/seqshot/sample_config.yaml - scripts/bench-summarize.py - tools/convert_snapshot_to_parquet.py

Testing and CI: CI job added (bench-e2e) that runs the integration test suite in a small containerized env. On first run the bench-e2e job failed due to a non-deterministic histogram merge edge case; fixed by adding stable bucket ordering and extra asserts. All unit tests and bench-e2e passed on the final push. Artifacts: compressed snapshot samples and stitched curve CSV were uploaded to PR artifacts for reviewer inspection.

Review conversation (trimmed): Arjun: "Nice shape — stitching algorithm looks sensible. Can we avoid keeping all snapshots in memory for long runs?" Author (Maya): "Good catch — added a rolling window writer that flushes intermediate aggregates to disk (serializer.py) and uses streaming merge in the reporter." Lucia: "Please add a small CLI flag to force single-cohort fast-path for very large scale runs." Author: "Added --fast-path-cohort and unit-tested the branch." Ben: "Integration test is a bit slow; can we parametrize to run with smaller window in CI?" Author: "CI now uses 10s windows vs 60s locally; documented in bench-e2e.yml."

Performance notes: In local microburst runs stitching reduced noisy p99 variance by ~18% vs naive union (artifact bench-results/seqshot_microburst.zip). Memory usage for a 1h run with 10 cohorts stayed under 1.2GB using streaming merge; peak memory reduced after rolling flush implemented.

Backward compatibility and migration: Snapshot format is additive; old reporters ignore new fields. The new reporter is an opt-in consumer; default bench pipelines unchanged. No breaking changes to public APIs.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main. Post-merge follow-ups tracked on ENG-2031 for further optimizations and a planned dashboard for stitched curves.
